en: The Sutra of the Names of the Thousand Buddhas of the Future Constellation Kalpa—also known as the Collection of the Great Merit-Mountains of All Buddhas—compiled during the Kaiyuan era as a supplement to the Liang dynasty records.
Now, when one cultivates goodness, blessings arrive; when one commits evil, calamities follow. The principles of reality are luminously clear, yet those who believe and awaken to them...

Alas! Since we have all been born together in this world of the five turbidities, the afflictions of the five aggregates and the three poisons blaze fiercely, causing us to revolve through birth and death without end.
Formerly, when the Buddha was in the world, the number of people was like the sands of the Ganges; now they have gradually declined until not even one in ten thousand remains. Why is this so?

It is because those who do good are few, while those who commit evil are many; upon death they fall into the three miserable realms, becoming entirely fish, insects, or animals, and no longer obtain a human body.
Therefore, the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* states:
"The three evil realms will be filled, while the hosts of devas and humans will diminish.
Before long, the kalpa will come to an end; this long-term decline is truly lamentable.

Therefore, the Tathāgata teaches according to circumstances, emphasizing compassion and valuing goodness; by not begrudging one’s own life and by practicing with diligent perseverance, one may attain liberation.
The slight labor of prostrating for a brief moment can eliminate the sins of immeasurable kalpas.
When sin is extinguished and merit arises, one attains the state of non-action (*asamskrta*).
Within this future Constellation Kalpa (*Nakṣatra-kalpa*), there shall be a thousand Buddhas appearing in the world; their names are as follows.

If a person hears this name and pays homage with single-minded devotion, without giving rise to indolence, they will surely attain nirvāṇa, forever leave behind the afflictions of birth and death within the three miserable realms, abide securely in loving-kindness and patience, and become fully endowed with extensive learning.

If there are those who can receive, uphold, practice, and recite it, such persons will certainly encounter a thousand Buddhas in succession; they shall obtain the extinction of the heavy sins of birth and death from immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas, and attain the supernatural powers, samādhis, and unimpeded eloquence of all Buddhas.

Regarding all the great Dharma-gates and dharani-gates, as well as the various wisdoms found in all scriptures, one should preach the Dharma according to what is appropriate without deceiving oneself. Remaining free from fame and profit, one should harbor no jealousy and practice the six points of respectful harmony;
upholding these with a single mind, one shall not lose this causal connection.
A practitioner who acts in this way will swiftly attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

If there are sons or daughters of noble family who, upon hearing the names of these Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, rejoice with faith and delight, upholding, reciting, and reading them without slandering them; or who are able to transcribe them and explain them to others; or who are able to fashion and erect their images; or who are able to make offerings of incense, flowers, and music, praising the Buddha’s merits and prostrating with a sincere heart—this is superior to using the lands of all the Buddhas in the ten directions, filling them with precious jewels and pure maṇi gems piled as high as the Brahma Heaven, and giving them as alms for hundreds of thousands of kalpas.

These sons and daughters of noble family have already made offerings to this Tathāgata in the past; having subsequently attained these merits in their future lives, they shall reach the state of Buddhahood without end, and all shall receive the prediction of enlightenment from the Buddhas of the Bhadrakalpa.

In whatever place that person is born, they will always encounter the Triple Gem and attain birth in the buddha-fields of all Buddhas. Their six sense faculties will be complete, they will not fall into the eight difficult conditions, and they will swiftly attain the full possession of the thirty-two major marks and eighty minor characteristics. If one can prostrate with the five limbs touching the ground even once, declaring aloud:
"I now universally pay homage to all Buddhas of the ten directions and the three periods of time," [the merit shall be as described].
One should remain [in this posture] until a thousand Buddhas have passed, after which one may then rise; the merit and blessings obtained will be as described above.

Taking this merit, one should vow that all sentient beings of the five realms who are subject to impermanence shall be born in the Land of Amitāyus Buddha, establishing a great vow to cause all sentient beings to be born in that realm.

Once born in that land, their physical marks and signs of excellence, as well as their wisdom and eloquence, shall be like those of the World-Honored One Amitābha; the karmic fruits they obtain shall likewise be equal to those of the World-Honored One.
